claims: "The class explores David's consolidation of power, including the establishment of his capital, building alliances, expanding his family, and waging successful battles against the Philistines." - While the class covers these topics, the teacher explicitly states that the list of children and the building of the palace are not in chronological order and did not happen immediately after the conquest of Jerusalem, contradicting the implication of a single consolidated timeline.

"Rabbi Tawil examines Shemuel Bet Chapter 5, covering David's coronation over all of Bnei Yisrael in Hebron" - The teacher clarifies that the coronation in Hebron over all of Israel happened at the end of the seven years of strife, not at the start of his reign in Hebron.
summary: Rabbi Tawil examines Shemuel Bet Chapter 5, covering David's coronation over all of Bnei Yisrael in Hebron and his subsequent conquest of Jerusalem from the Yevusi. The class explores David's consolidation of power, including the establishment of his capital, building alliances, expanding his family, and waging successful battles against the Philistines.
questions: Why did David choose Jerusalem as his capital city after ruling in Hebron?
How does the account of conquering Jerusalem in Shemuel differ from the parallel text in Divrei HaYamim?
What role did the water shaft play in the conquest of Jerusalem?
Why did the Philistines attack David only after he became king over all of Bnei Yisrael?
